- **★★★★ CORRECTED WITHIN THIS FILING — I FILED A CONSUMING PROJECT'S WRONG
  DIAGNOSIS AS PDFCE'S OWN FACT, AND THE NEXT STEP WAS TO PUBLISH IT BACK TO
  THEM IN `docs/core-api/`.** What the dispatch relayed and this filing first
  recorded, kept legible: ~~"`TextRun::text` contains characters that are not
  in the file — extraction synthesises a space wherever a `TJ` offset exceeds
  the word-gap threshold, so a title-block cell reads `"FINISH         "`
  while the buffer holds `FINISH` and kerning numbers."~~ **FALSE.** A
  derived word space is **never inside a glyph run**:
  `text_extract/layout.rs`'s `Break::Word` arm calls `close_run()` and *then*
  `emit_derived(' ', TextOrigin::DerivedWordSpace)`, pushing a **separate
  one-character `TextRun` with `glyphs: Vec::new()`**; `text_edit/model.rs:548`
  keeps them apart on the edit side too. **World-source (hard rule 10's
  corollary — a correction is a claim):** the engineer measured every run
  from **256 fixture PDFs** via `pdfce-cli extract-text --json` —
  `derived_word_space` runs **5**; glyph runs containing a synthesised space
  **0** (the claimed cause); glyph runs where `len(text) != len(glyphs)`
  **1**. Their `"FINISH         "` is almost certainly **their own
  concatenation** of a glyph run + a `DerivedWordSpace` run + a glyph run.
- **★★★ THE SINGLE OFFENDER IS THE REAL MECHANISM, AND NEITHER SIDE HAD IT.**
  `fixtures/synthetic/text/identity-h-tounicode.pdf`: one run, **8 characters
  over 6 glyphs**. **`/ToUnicode` maps one glyph to several characters**
  (ISO 32000-1 §9.10.3) — an `ffl` ligature is one glyph and three
  characters, a surrogate pair one glyph and two `char`s. **So their headline
  claim was TRUE and their mechanism WRONG**, and the two differ in
  consequence: synthesis would insert a character in **no** operator, while a
  ligature maps a character **range** onto a glyph that **is** in the
  operator — so a `find` built from `TextRun::text` fails on the **buffer
  bytes**, not on locating the operator. **Invisible on unligatured test
  text; routine on real typeset copy.** `Pass 145.0`'s docs half is
  re-scoped accordingly: `TextRun::text`'s docs owe *"one glyph may map to
  several characters, so `text.chars().count()` is not `glyphs.len()`"* —
  **not** the *"may contain derived characters"* line originally asked for,
  which would have shipped a false statement to the project that reported it.
- **★★ `CLAUDE.md` RULE 4, RESTATED ON THE CORRECTED FACTS.** The original
  note here argued the synthesised space was an undisclosed-where-you-look
  inference. On the true facts: the `/ToUnicode` expansion is **not an
  inference at all** (it is the file's own mapping), and the derived word
  space **is** disclosed as an **entire separate run** tagged
  `TextOrigin::DerivedWordSpace` — a stronger disclosure than credited. The
  `R220` findability point survives only in weakened form, on the
  glyph-count fact.
- **★ A `TextRun` SPANNING SEVERAL SHOW OPERATORS — RECORDED AS UNVERIFIED,
  NOT AS CONFIRMED.** The requester's third cause: `layout` closes a run on
  geometry, a producer closes an operator wherever its writer felt like it;
  their symptom, *"eleven pieces of text went bold and the twelfth refused"*
  on a page where nothing is unusual. **Not measured here and not measurable
  from outside:** `GlyphProvenance::operator_span` is **not exposed** by
  `pdfce-cli extract-text --json` (glyph objects carry `code`/`rung`/
  `sourced`/`start`/`len`/`x`/`y`/`advance`/`size`/`direction`/`invisible`
  and no span). **The method that would settle it, written down because it is
  owed either way:** an **in-crate probe over a corpus counting runs whose
  glyphs carry more than one distinct `model.provenance(...).operator_span`.
  **★ One probe, two answers** — it also settles the `operator_span`-slice
  invariant of `Pass 145.0` criterion 3.
- **★ AN INVARIANT QUESTION IS OWED WHICHEVER WAY `Pass 145.0` GOES.** The
  requester's fallback ask is a documented invariant — *"the glyphs sharing
  one `operator_span` always slice a contiguous, matchable range out of the
  run's text"* — which they *"believe is true today"* and *"have no way to
  know whether it is guaranteed."* **Only pdfce can answer it, and the two
  outcomes are not symmetric:** if it holds it is undocumented load-bearing
  behaviour needing a test; **if it does not, their shipped workaround is

- **★ A DOWNSTREAM TEST WILL BREAK ON PURPOSE AND THEY ASKED FOR THAT.**
  `pdfceGUI`'s Bold button retries with the face the refusal names; they

- **★ DECISION 058 WORKING FROM THE OTHER SIDE.** The requester declined to

**Decisions made this session:**

- **★★★ DECISION 094 MINTED — the `operator_span`-slice invariant is a
  GUARANTEE pdfce publishes, not an implementation detail; and
  `ARCHITECTURE.md` gains §4.2, *Published model guarantees*, as the place
  such things live.** The 296th filing's `Pass 145.0` entry named this a
  decision-log candidate **conditional on the invariant holding**. It held, so
  the condition discharged and the record was owed.
  **The decision is not "the invariant is true" — measurement established
  that. The decision is to PROMISE it**, and the promise costs something:
  `text_extract/layout.rs`'s run segmentation may no longer be refactored so
  that one group's glyphs become non-contiguous within a run, **even if no
  pdfce feature notices**. pdfce's own code could absorb such a change with
  every test green; only a shell would break. §4.2's entry format is fixed at
  four parts — the property, the measurement, the test that pins it, and **the
  refactor it forbids** — because a guarantee without its measurement is a
  claim, and one without its forbidden refactor does not tell a future
  engineer what they may not do.
  **Why a new §4.2 rather than a line in §4.1:** §4.1 is a *sync* section,
  written to be **replaced** when it drifts; a guarantee is binding and
  append-only, and burying one in a document whose contract is *"rewrite me
  when I go stale"* would eventually delete it by routine maintenance.
- **DECISION DECLINED, recorded so the absence is not read as an oversight:
  `accept_font_target` as the single acceptance predicate is NOT a decision
  record.** It is a correct **application of `R221`** to a new subsystem, not
  a new boundary, crate split, library choice or invariant definition. Filing
  every correct application of a standing rule as a decision would make the
  log a duplicate of *Shipped*. Precedent: the 295th filing declined on
  exactly this ground.
- **★★ STANDING RULE `R223` MINTED — a doc comment's claim about its own
  CALLERS is a measurement, and nothing recompiles when it goes stale;
  re-derive it by running the grep it quotes, never by reasoning about what
  changed.** Distinct from `R93` (a comment wrong about the code beside it)
  and from `R222` (a claim duplicated into a format string): here the
  **truth-maker lives outside the documented item entirely**, in the set of
  its callers, so **the person who falsifies it never reads it**, `cargo doc`
  cannot check it, and it is **almost always true when written** — the defect
  is in the claim's *form*, not its author's diligence.
  **★ The mint's warrant is better than a count.** Instance 1
  (`crates/pdfce-core/src/ocr/layer.rs` — a doc comment wrong about its own
  callers **three times in one session**, the third produced *while correcting
  the second*) was **explicitly declined** promotion by this role, on the

  Clause (c) is the one worth carrying: **prefer moving the claim somewhere a
  compiler can hold it.** `Pass 144.0`'s own remedy is the worked example —

- **★★★ THE INVARIANT HOLDS, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE ENTRY.**

  groups (1.58 per run, 22.9 glyphs per group) → 0 non-contiguous, 0 failing

  2,420 of 18,559 runs (13.0 %) carry glyphs from more than one show

- **★★ TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY RUNNING THE BINARY, NOT BY A 4,463-TEST SUITE,
  BOTH IN THIS SESSION'S OWN NEW CODE.** `cmd_edit_text` **parsed
  `--pin-span` and never attached it** — the refusal read *"empty find text"*,
  exactly what the feature removes, and **every unit test passed** because
  they exercise the core API directly. And a shipped refusal string carried
  **fourteen baked-in spaces** past a green `check-string-gaps.sh`.
  **Generalisable half:** both live in the **shell layer between the flags and
  the core API** — the one layer a core-API test cannot exercise by
  construction. Driving the release binary is the only instrument that covers
  it.
- **★★★ `check-string-gaps.sh` UNDER-REPORTED FOR THE THIRD TIME AND IS FIXED
  AS A CLASS, WITH THE WIDENING'S SCOPE CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT.** Its own
  header says the previous repair *"widens both ends of the class rather than
  only the end that failed"* — and it widened both ends to `{`/`}` and
  stopped. The next miss had **two holes at once**: the literal was an
  `eprintln!` rather than an `#[error(...)]` so **prose mode never ran**, and
  even in prose mode the trailing class **did not admit a hyphen** — when the
  next word after a gap in a CLI diagnostic is, more than anything else, a
  `--flag`. Fixed by a structural argument about the string's **role**: a
  literal opening with the binary's own diagnostic prefix (`"pdfce-cli: "` /
  `"pdfce-gui: "`) is a sentence an operator reads, never an aligned report
  column. **Measured before widening: blanket → 24 findings, ~18 of them
  legitimate (DXF byte streams, aligned probe columns); scoped to prose → 1,
  the defect.** A self-test fixture for the shape was added.
  **Transferable statement, now three for three: in prose mode the trailing
  class is *"anything that starts a word"*, not a list of the characters that
  have failed so far.** Same shape as `R220`'s three-deep escalation — **a
  repair that generalises to the instance rather than to the class schedules
  its own successor.**
- **★ A NEW FIXTURE WAS REQUIRED AND NOBODY HAD PREDICTED IT.** Nothing in the
  corpus carried **two resources with one `/BaseFont`** — the 87 % case the

- **★ AN O(n²) SCAN OVER AN ATTACKER-CONTROLLED `/Font` DICT, FIXED WHILE

  ~50,000 a crafted one can** — in a query the requester has since confirmed

**★★ The mechanism is NOT "the channel moved", and that shallow reading is
what the amendment blocks.** The 297th filing **ran `ls -lt`** — its own box

filing **read the file its box was about**, and quoted it **to substantiate a
claim about the present**, without recording **when** that reading was taken.
⇢ ***A directory listing is not a reading. `ls -lt` tells you a file exists;

without carrying it**. **A cautious `[ ]` would have been less wrong and more
honest**, because nothing would have been asserted that could go stale. ⇢
***Substantiating a claim raises its confidence without raising its shelf
life.*** `R220`(c)'s four prior instances had shelf lives of hours to days;

**Standing rules amended in place — three, no ceiling movement:**

- **★★ `R203` GAINS CLAUSE (d) — a citation substantiating a `gui` box is a
  TIMESTAMPED READING of a file, not a fact.** Obliges three things: name the
  file, its mtime **and the time the reading was taken**; **read every channel
  file newer than the one you are quoting before you quote it** (bounded by the
  listing you have already run); and **prefer the bare checkbox to a stale
  quotation** — a `[ ]` with no sentence decays quietly, a `[ ]` with a
  quotation decays **loudly and with a citation**, which a later reader trusts
  harder. **No gate proposed and none is possible**, on `R203`'s founding
  warrant: a gate would have to know what the other project's build currently
  does, which is the fact the claim exists to report.
- **★★ `R209` GAINS CLAUSE (e) — a gate-sweep figure owes its DENOMINATOR.**
  *"13 gates green"* is **not** naming the set; it is a **count**, and a count
  without its population **cannot disagree with anything**. It reads as
  compliance with clause (a) while satisfying none of its purpose. Every sweep
  figure is now written **`N of M`** — **and a relayed figure is re-expressed
  with its denominator by whoever relays it**, which is this role, constantly,
  and the last cheap place to add it.
  **★★★ THE MECHANICAL REMEDY SHIPPED WHILE THIS CLAUSE WAS BEING DRAFTED,
  INDEPENDENTLY: `tools/run-gates.sh` (`1e62715`)** — and it is better than the
  one this role was about to recommend. It derives its list from
  `check-ci-parity.py --list`, i.e. **from the WORKFLOW, not from the
  directory**, so a new CI job appears in the runner with no edit to the
  runner; **the filing gates run LAST by construction**; it does not stop at
  the first failure; the two skipped commands are **named**.
  **★★ The two denominators are RECONCILED rather than left side by side** —
  this clause must not commit the error it was minted over. This role measured
  **19 scripts on disk, 6 omitted**; the engineer measured **25 commands, 5
  omitted**. **Both correct, different sets**: the script population includes a
  file CI does not run and **excludes every non-script command CI does**
  (`cargo fmt`, clippy, wasm32, `--no-default-features`, the fuzz check). **The
  workflow-derived list is the better denominator**, for `R209`'s founding
  reason: *"the gates are green"* is only interesting relative to what CI will
  run. ⇢ **Quote `N of M` from `run-gates.sh`, not from `ls`.**
  **★★ And running the list found a defect IN the list on its first run**: the
  `cargo tree` GUI-denylist command had an **inverted exit sense** — `grep`
  exits 1 on no match, which is the passing condition — so it **reported
  failure on a healthy tree and SUCCESS ON A VIOLATED ONE**, the worse
  direction. **It survived because nothing had ever RUN the list; it was read
  and retyped.** ⇢ ***Giving a documented list a CONSUMER is what turns its
  errors into red lines.*** Corrected, and **widened to both crates because CI
  checks both**. A **third dangling gate reference** (`run-all.sh`, cited in
  `check-string-gaps.sh`'s header, never on disk) was **made true rather than
  struck**. ⇢ *A reference inside a trusted document is indistinguishable from
  a real one until somebody runs `ls`.*
  **★★ The engineer reached this finding independently within the same hour**,

  not** — `ls tools/check-*` is one command in this repository, and it would

  file a total beside its denominator — arriving where hard rule 10 was not
  written to cover: somebody else's sweep, quoted in a commit message.*
- **★★ THE PASS'S DESIGN IS SET BY A REFUSAL, and it is `CLAUDE.md` rule 4 read
  correctly from OUTSIDE the project.** *"Just default to Solid 1 pt"* would
  have worked and would have been wrong: **a properties control has to show the
  CURRENT value**, and seeded from a default it would show *Solid, 1 pt* over a
  widget whose file says *Dashed, 3 pt* — **and the operator's first press
  would write the invention into their document.** They cited pdfce's own
  `DeviceCMYK`-swatch precedent for the refusal, correctly, and **shipped the
  pane with the two controls ABSENT** (`R9`) rather than fill them.
  ⇢ **`border: None` MEANS THE FILE STATES NO BORDER and is NOT
  `BorderSpec::default()`** — that default is solid/1 pt **because it
  reproduces the bytes pdfce has always AUTHORED**: **correct for a writer, a
  lie from a reader.** Escalated to `C:/personal_rag/pdf/` this filing.
- **★ THE TWO PLACES A DEFAULT *IS* APPLIED, and the distinction is the whole
  design.** A `/BS` present but missing `/W` takes Table 166's default of 1 —
  **the file has COMMITTED to having a border by carrying a `/BS`**, so filling
  in the width the standard specifies is **reading**; **inventing** is
  producing a border for a widget carrying **neither key**. Same shape for
  `/Border`'s dash array: it is the **only** discriminator the array form has,
  so Dashed-when-non-empty is a **faithful reading**, not an inference. **Width
  0 is a VALUE** (Table 166 says *"no border"*), never an absence. **`/F`
  absent is 0, which IS one of the four (`ScreenOnly`)** — so a `None`
  visibility always means *present and unmappable*, never *absent*.
- **★★ THE CLI TESTS ARE ROUND TRIPS, NOT FIXTURE READS, AND THE REASON
  GENERALISES.** The defect was an **asymmetry between a writer and a reader**,
  and **only a test that drives both halves can pin an asymmetry**: `edit-widget
  --border-style dashed --border-width 3` then `list-fields --widgets` must
  report `border=D/3.00`. A hand-authored fixture tests the reader against
  bytes **the author chose**; this tests it against bytes **pdfce chose**,
  which is the pair that has to agree. ⇢ *When the defect is a disagreement
  between two code paths, a fixture pins one path and proves nothing about the
  pair.*
- **★ NO FORM FIXTURE IN THE CORPUS CARRIES A BORDER AT ALL — measured HERE.**
  `ls -1 fixtures/synthetic/forms/*.pdf | wc -l` → **11**; `grep -l "/BS"` →
  **0**; `grep -l "/Border"` → **0**. **Zero of eleven on both keys.** No
  fixture was added and **none was needed** — the round-trip design is what
  made one unnecessary. **Contrast the 297th filing**, where `format_twins.pdf`
  had to be minted. The two decisions are opposite and both correct: *a fixture
  is owed when the READER must face bytes pdfce would not write, and not owed
  when the property under test is that a writer and a reader agree.*
- **★ SABOTAGE.** Making an absent border return `BorderSpec::default()` — the
  design the requester refused — turns **2 of the 12** unit tests red,
  **including the one named for it**. The mutation was chosen to be **the
  defect the Pass exists to prevent** rather than an arbitrary one.
- **★★ THE CONSUMER'S FOUR CLAIMS ABOUT OUR CRATE WERE CHECKED AND ALL FOUR

## 2026-08-28 (299th filing) — `Pass 147.0` (`8aa9cea`) SHIPS: **a query built to stop a shell offering unusable fonts became an UNCONDITIONAL YES** — `preview_font_resources(page, "", Some(pin))` checked **zero characters** and reported every face on the page as `Accepted`; ★★★★★ **and this filing's hard-rule-11 sweep found the SAME DEFECT STILL LIVE ONE FUNCTION OVER** — `preview_style_resolution`, the query that decides where a Bold button routes, is the one entry point of three that never calls `effective_find`, **reported by nobody, found by searching for the CLAIM**; ★★★★ **the cause was two Passes shipping out of step, so two functions took the same two operands and disagreed about what an empty one MEANS** — `R221`'s **fourth** instance, and **the first found by a CONSUMER rather than from inside**; ★★★ **both of the reporter's offered remedies were needed and the engineer had one** — an unpinned empty `find` was also vacuous, because `find_anchor` runs `s.text.contains(find)` and **every string contains the empty string**, making it the MORE reachable half; ★★ **`R219` gains clause (e) — the enumeration's answers must be MEASURED, not RECALLED** — and the *"verify each instance, not the class"* mint is **DECLINED with three reasons and a revisit trigger**, because minting a rule that duplicates a live memory file would be two descriptions of one rule, which is `R221`'s own subject; ★ **the channel check ran FIRST and came back clean for the first time in five filings**

**Dispatch:** *"roadmap update — pass shipped"*, from `pdfce-engineer`, with the
exact tip hash supplied (`8aa9cea`) and an explicit instruction to run the
channel check **first** per `R203`(d).

**Shipped:**

- **`Pass 147.0`** (`8aa9cea`) — `preview_font_resources(page, "", Some(pin))`
  located the right operator, checked **zero characters**, and reported **every
  face on the page as `Accepted`**, including one that provably cannot show the
  run. Fixed by calling `effective_find` — the same function `plan_format`
  calls — and by **refusing** an unpinned empty `find`. CLI:
  `font-preflight --pin-span START:LEN`, `--find` now optional.

**★★★★★ THE FINDING THIS FILING PRODUCED THAT NOBODY DISPATCHED: THE SAME
DEFECT IS STILL LIVE ONE FUNCTION OVER.**

The hard-rule-11 sweep asked *"what else takes `(find, pinned_span)` and decides
something from the caller's string?"* — the **claim**, not the identifier — and
found **`EditSession::preview_style_resolution`** (`edit.rs:7388` →
`format.rs:2635`), the query that decides **where a Bold button routes**.

- **`grep -n "effective_find" crates/pdfce-core/src/text_edit/format.rs` returns
  exactly two call sites**: `1514` (`plan_format`, the commit path) and `3197`
  (`preview_font_resources`, added by this Pass). **There is no third.**
- `preview_style_resolution` builds its locating `EditRequest` with
  `find: find.to_owned()` (`2654`) and passes the **raw** string to
  `probe_synthesis` at three sites (`2681`, `2688`, `2699`) →
  `gate_synthesis` → **`survey_page_fonts(..., text)` at `2395`** — *the same
  call whose vacuity was this Pass's defect, at the other of its two call
  sites*.
- **Both halves are present.** Pinned + empty: every candidate surveys as
  accepted, so it answers `RealFaceResolves` naming a face that then refuses.
  Unpinned + empty: `contains("")` matches the **first show operator on the
  page**.
- **★★ The consequence is WORSE here than in the pre-flight.** A pre-flight
  returns a **list**, and a universal yes offers faces that later refuse. This
  returns a **routing decision**, so a wrong `RealFaceResolves` sends Bold to
  `set_font` on a refusing face — **no bold by either route**, which is
  `R221`'s *third*-instance cost profile (a capability removed), not its
  fourth's (a richer-looking list).
- **Scope, checked:** public `EditSession` method, **no CLI subcommand**, so the
  reachable consumer is a library caller — `pdfceGUI`, which drives its
  Bold/Italic buttons from exactly this query. **The commit path is unaffected
  and correct.**
- **REPORTED, NOT EDITED** (`crates/` is outside this role's remit). A ★★★★★
  *Next up* box is open with **no Pass ID claimed** and four proposed acceptance
  criteria. **Next free family `148`.**

**⇒ The transferable sentence:** ***a route enumeration scoped to the FUNCTION
being fixed is scoped to the instance, not the class.*** `Pass 147.0` enumerated
the pinned and unpinned *branches* of the function it was fixing — and did it
well, catching a defect that way — while the sibling **function** taking the
same two operands went unasked **in the commit that was about exactly this
hazard**.

**★ Every prior hard-rule-11 sweep in this file turned up WORDING that had gone
false. This one turned up EXECUTABLE CODE with the same bug the Pass was
closing** — the strongest evidence yet for the rule's *search-for-the-claim*
clause, since a grep for `preview_font_resources` returns
`preview_style_resolution` **zero** times.

**Findings + decisions:**

- **★★ THE FAILURE WAS SILENT AND INVERTED, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS A PASS AND NOT
  A DOC LINE.** The list looks **richer**, not broken — nothing errors, nothing
  logs, and the query built to stop a shell offering unusable faces became the
  thing producing the refusal. **Strictly worse than the `fontinfo` name-join
  superset it replaced**, which was at least a superset of the page's fonts by
  name. ⇒ *"Returns more than it should" is a HIGH-severity failure mode for an
  ACCEPTANCE query, even though it is benign for a filter.*
- **★★ THE CAUSE WAS TWO PASSES SHIPPING OUT OF STEP, in the engineer's own
  words: "one I created by shipping two Passes out of step."** `Pass 145.0` gave
  an empty `find` on a pinned request a **new meaning** and told callers so;
  `Pass 142.1`'s pre-flight kept passing the caller's string verbatim. ⇒ ***A
  release note that gives an operand a new meaning is an `R221` trigger for
  every sibling function taking that operand***, and that sweep belongs in the
  Pass that changes the meaning — not in the bug report four hours later, and
  not in the sweep two filings later (which is where the survivor above came
  from).
- **★★ BOTH OF THE REPORTER'S REMEDIES WERE NEEDED AND THEY WERE READ AS AN
  EITHER/OR.** Remedy (1) *resolve from the anchor* closes the **pinned** route;
  remedy (2) *refuse by name* closes the **unpinned** route. Neither closes
  both. The engineer shipped (1), assumed the unpinned case already errored —
  **and a test written expecting to pass proved otherwise**: `find_anchor` with
  no pin runs `s.text.contains(find)`, and **every string contains the empty
  string**. ⇒ *When a reporter offers two remedies for one symptom, check
  whether they cover different reachability ROUTES before choosing between
  them.* And: **the unpinned half is the more reachable one**, since it is
  reached *by accident* rather than by following guidance.
- **★★ THE DECISIVE TEST IS AN EQUALITY, NOT A CORRECTNESS CHECK.** One CLI test
  asserts the **pinned-empty and explicit-`find` JSON outputs are
  BYTE-IDENTICAL** for the same operator. A test asserting *"the pinned-empty
  query now returns the right verdicts"* would pass if the two paths were fixed
  separately and happened to agree today. ⇒ *When the defect is a DISAGREEMENT
  between two paths, the oracle is EQUALITY OF THE TWO OUTPUTS, not correctness
  of one* — the mirror of the 298th filing's *"a fixture pins one path and
  proves nothing about the pair"*.
- **★ SABOTAGE THAT DISCRIMINATES BEATS SABOTAGE THAT REDDENS EVERYTHING.**
  Reverting to the caller's string turns **2 of 13** core tests red **and leaves
  the unpinned-refusal test GREEN** — correct, since it exercises the other
  half. A mutation turning all 13 red would have shown the tests are coupled to
  the *file*, not the *behaviour*. The engineer reported the green as a
  **result**, not a worry; named here so a later session does not "fix" it.
- **★ THE WIDENED GATE FROM `1e62715` MADE ITS FIRST REAL CATCH ON ITS FIRST
  REAL CHANCE.** `check-string-gaps.sh` caught a lost line continuation **in a
  new test, before it shipped.** The previous instance of that class

  found by a librarian sweep afterwards. ⇒ `R209`(e)'s pay-off, with a live
  catch rather than a rationale.
- **★ 187 of the 325 changed lines are test lines** (`git show --stat 8aa9cea`,

- **`R221` — fourth instance, amended in place.** New information, not a tally:
  **the first instance found by a CONSUMER rather than from inside**, and the
  first where the two drifting descriptions were **a resolution step and a
  parameter list** rather than two predicates. Also recorded there: applying
  `R221` to a function's **body** does not apply it to its **signature**, and

  `preview_style_resolution` survivor above.]**
- **`R219` — NEW CLAUSE (e): the enumeration's answers must be MEASURED, not
  RECALLED.** Every prior `R219` instance is a route that went **unasked**. This
  is the first where a route was **asked and mis-answered**. The asymmetry that
  makes the clause cheap: *"route B is broken too"* is self-checking — you fix
  it and the fix proves it; *"route B is fine"* is **unfalsifiable without an
  instrument**, leaves no trace in the diff, and reads in review as diligence.
  **The negative answer is the one that needs the test.** Watch for the phrase
  *"this already errors"* / *"unchanged, and it must stay unchanged"* — a belief
  stated in the register of a fact.

  argued rather than defaulted.** Three reasons, in order of weight: (1) the

**★★★★★ PROVENANCE IS THE HEADLINE: THIS ROLE'S 299th-FILING SWEEP FOUND A LIVE
DEFECT NOBODY DISPATCHED IT TO LOOK FOR, AND IT WAS THE WORST OF THE THREE.**

Every prior hard-rule-11 sweep in this file turned up **wording** that had gone
false — a doc comment, a `println!`, a `FEATURES.md` row, a table header. The
299th's turned up **executable code carrying the same bug the Pass it was filing
had just closed**, and `Pass 148.0` is that finding shipped, four hours later.

- **The engineer reproduced it before believing it** — three probe calls on
  `fixtures/synthetic/textedit/format_family.pdf`, tabulated in the Shipped
  entry. **Every particular of the analysis held, including the "worse than the
  pre-flight" judgement**, which was the part most open to being read as
  rhetoric. ⇒ Recorded against `R203`: **the reproduce-before-believing
  obligation attaches to the CLAIM, not to who filed it**, and a report from
  inside the project is if anything *more* likely to be waved through.
- **A `grep` for `preview_font_resources` returns `preview_style_resolution`
  zero times.** Nothing textual connected them. What connected them was the
  question *"what else decides something from the caller's string?"* — the
  strongest evidence yet for hard rule 11's **search-for-the-claim** clause.
- **Filed as a boundary, not a boast:** the sweep is a *reading*, and it worked
  here because the meaning-change was fresh in the same filing. **The instrument
  is the half that will still be working next month**, which is why `R224`'s
  second clause is about the instrument and not about the reading.

**Findings + decisions:**

- **★★ WHY THIS INSTANCE WAS WORSE, AND IT IS WHY IT IS ITS OWN PASS.**
  `preview_font_resources` returns a **LIST** — a wrong entry is one row an
  operator can look past, and pressing it yields a named refusal.
  `preview_style_resolution` returns a **ROUTING DECISION** — `WouldSynthesize`
  vs `RealFaceResolves` — so a wrong `RealFaceResolves` sends the Bold button to
  `set_font` on a refusing face **and suppresses the synthesis fallback**. ⇒
  **No bold by either route**, i.e. `R221`'s *third*-instance cost profile (a
  capability removed), not its fourth's (a richer-looking list).
- **★★ THE JUDGEMENT THIS ROLE FLAGGED AS THE ENGINEER'S WAS MADE, AND ITS
  SECOND ARGUMENT IS THE TRANSFERABLE ONE.** Refusing an unpinned empty `find`
  is a **behaviour change for an existing caller**. The engineer shipped it on
  two arguments: an error beats a wrong answer about an operator nobody named
  (*about this call*), and *"a third behaviour across five entry points would be
  a third thing to remember"* (*about the set*). ⇒ ***When a change would give
  one member of a uniform set a third behaviour, count the cost against the SET,
  not against the member*** — the member-local reading always makes the third
  behaviour look like the smaller change.
- **★★ THE INSTRUMENT, AND ITS FAILED FIRST CUT IS THE FINDING.** Test 2 of
  `route_enumeration.rs` asserts **every function calling `find_anchor` also
  calls `effective_find`** — a source scan, and *the only assertion in the file
  that can fail on a route added after the test was written*; test 1's behaviour
  sweep over four entry points is **bounded by the list somebody remembered**.
  The scan's first cut used a **30-line window** and **reported all four
  known-good sites as violations** (the resolution legitimately sits 70+ lines
  later). ⇒ ***A gate with a tuning parameter has exactly one direction of
  travel under pressure — looser*** — so the unit became the **function body**,
  which the language already defines. **★ And the bad heuristic failed LOUDLY,
  which is the only reason it was replaced: a lenient one passes forever and is
  indistinguishable from a working gate.** Write the strict version first.
- **★ THREE DETAILS THAT KEEP A SOURCE SCAN HONEST**, read here in the test
  source rather than taken from the commit message: a **floor**
  (`callers.len() >= 4`), because a scan goes **vacuous rather than red** when
  its anchor is renamed; a **named exemption list, empty at birth**, whose
  entries are claims reviewable in a diff (*"widen it by name, with a reason —
  do not delete the test"*); and **exclusion of the definition and of `///`
  mentions**, whose false positives are what push a later reader to loosen.
- **★ A `ResolvedFind` NEWTYPE WAS DECLINED ON THE RECORD, IN THE TEST'S OWN
  MODULE DOC** — *"it changes four signatures to prevent a class that has now
  been closed, and the cheap detector comes first."* ⇒ *Reach for the type on
  the second firing.* Recorded so a later session reads the absence as a
  decision.
- **★ SABOTAGE THAT REDDENS THE STRUCTURAL ASSERTION IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN
  `Pass 147.0`'s.** Removing the `effective_find` call turns **3 of the 4** new
  tests red **including the source scan** — which proves the scan is *coupled to
  the property*, not merely present. The one staying green is the
  unpinned-refusal test, the correct discrimination since it exercises the other
  half. **A source scan that stays green under a mutation of the thing it scans
  for is a scan whose anchor has drifted** — the failure the floor exists for.

### ★★★ THE PROCESS NOTE — RECORDED AGAINST THE ENGINEER AT HIS OWN REQUEST, AND KEPT AS A NOTE RATHER THAN MINTED AS A RULE

He very nearly filed finding 2 as a **correction to `Pass 143.0`'s scoping** —
*"the filed cause is incomplete; the real problem is that there is no spot
plane."* **That would have been wrong, and wrong in the confident direction**,
which is the expensive kind: a correction arrives labelled *verified* and is
believed harder than what it replaced (hard rule 10's corollary). He caught it
by asking **what the four planes actually contain at paint time** instead of
stopping at *"the spot rule is unreachable, therefore the spot is unhandled."*

**⇒ A measurement that surprises you is not automatically a correction to the
thing you were measuring.** It may be a **second, unrelated fact that happens
to touch the same module.** Here, the two findings are not even in tension —
**one explains why the other is not a blocker on the first.**

**Disposition: NOTE, not a standing rule, and the decline is argued.** Three
reasons. **(a) It has n=1 in this project** — the near-miss did not land, and a
rule minted on an averted error has no falsifier to point at. **(b) The
existing rules already reach the failure it would have caused, from both
sides**: hard rule 10's corollary makes *a correction a claim* with the same
sourcing bar as what it corrects, and `R219`(e) requires an enumeration's
answers to be **measured rather than recalled** — the very act that caught it.
**(c) What is genuinely new here is a habit of INFERENCE, not of procedure**,
and this project has already paid for minting rules that duplicate a live
carrier (`R221`'s own subject, and the 299th filing's declined mint). **Revisit
trigger, stated so this decline is checkable:** a **second** instance in which a
scoping measurement is written up as a correction to its own subject and turns
out to be an independent fact ⇒ mint it, with both instances named. **Ceiling
unchanged at `R224`; next free `R225`.**

`check-cited-commits-exist.py`.** `eab7da4` and `fa16819` are cited above as
evidence and are **unreachable objects** — no branch, no tag, reflog-only. That
gate resolves citations with **`git cat-file -t`** (line 215, read here), which
answers *"does this object exist?"*, **not** *"is it reachable?"* — so this
entry passes **today** (verified, exit 0) and will **fail** once `git gc` prunes
them. ⇢ *A gate built to protect cited hashes cannot distinguish existence from
reachability, and this is the first filing to cite hashes that are the first and
not the second.* Disposition is the engineer's: teach the gate to report an
unreachable citation as a **warning naming the reason**, or exempt the two
tokens by name. **What must not happen is a future session reading a red gate on
this entry as a corrupt record** — the objects were always unreachable; **the
reflog table is the evidence, not the objects.** Reported as owed work.

**⇢ The correction STRENGTHENS the commit rather than undermining it,** and that
is the reading to carry. One harmless near-miss found by luck is a thin warrant
for new machinery. **A behaviour that recurred inside the same minute — after
the first occurrence had already been noticed and hand-recovered — is not a
near-miss. It is a repeating action nobody is announcing**, and the second one
landed on the commit type whose entire content is hash citations.

**★★★ AND THE SECOND RECOVERY IS THE GATE'S OWN ADVICE, EXECUTED BEFORE THE
GATE EXISTED.** The reflog line is literally `reset: moving to origin/main` at

minutes later**, and the remedy it prints is `git reset --mixed origin/main`.

missing was not knowledge but **announcement** — and that is exactly the half a
gate supplies and a rule does not.* This is the load-bearing argument behind

### WHAT SHIPPED IN `c087d47`

`tools/check-history-not-rewritten.py` (152 lines new, **68 of them module
docstring**) asks **one question: is `origin/main` an ancestor of `HEAD`?**
Yes → published history plus zero or more commits, the only shape an ordinary
fast-forward push can produce and the only shape decision **090**'s standing
*"always push"* covers. No → rewritten: it **names the orphaned commits**
(precisely the hashes documents may cite) and prints `git reset --mixed
origin/main`, **never `--force`**. It **does not fetch** (a gate that reaches
the network fails on a train; a stale `origin/main` can only make it lenient),
**does not object to being behind**, and treats **no remote / no remote branch
as a clean pass that SAYS SO** rather than passing silently. Exit `0` / `1` /
`2`. Wired into `tools/run-gates.sh` **FIRST**, because its failure invalidates
the meaning of everything after it.

### ★ MINTING — NOTHING MINTED, BOTH CANDIDATES ARGUED

**(a) *"a subagent can rewrite published history without announcing it"* —
DECLINED**, and the engineer's own objection is the right one: it would be a
**second description of a mechanical gate**, which is `R221`'s subject. Three
further reasons:
1. **The prohibition already exists.** Project rule 8 forbids `--force` and any
   history-rewriting push **by name**, with the fourteen-orphan precedent
   attached. A rule would be the **third** description.
2. **A rule cannot bind this failure mode.** Neither amend was a decision to
   rewrite published history — both were an `--amend` reflex by an agent that
   did not know the commit was published. *A rule asks an actor not to do what
   it does not know it is doing; the gate asks the tree a question with one
   answer.*
3. **The evidence says knowledge was never the missing input** — see the
   05:50:52Z recovery above, made correctly, by hand, 71 minutes before the gate
   existed.

**(b) *"a check CI structurally cannot perform belongs in the pre-push sweep,
and its absence from `check-ci-parity.py` is deliberate"* — DECLINED AS A RULE**,
because it is **already recorded in the three places a reader actually arrives
from**, each read here: the gate's docstring (*"which is why it is not in
`check-ci-parity.py`'s list"*), `run-gates.sh`'s comment at the invocation site
(lines 170–186), and `--list`'s printed banner *"pre-flight, first; CI cannot
check this one"*. A rule would be a **fourth** description.
⇢ ***The real gap this candidate points at is not a missing rule — it is the
stale header sentence in the survivors table above.*** Fixing one sentence
removes the hazard; minting a rule leaves the false sentence in place and adds a
thing that can drift from it.

**Ledger:** no Pass ID; **no decision minted, `095` next free**; **no standing
rule minted, ceiling stays `R224`, next free `R225`**; next free filing ordinal
**303**.

## 2026-08-28 (304th filing) — `Pass 150.0` (`943d482`) ships note text on markup — ★★★★★ **but the feature is not the finding: a test written for the new WRITE path failed, the engineer switched which encoder he called, it went GREEN — and that was a workaround for somebody else's bug hidden by a passing test. Measured properly, both encoders were correct and the DECODER was at fault, and `annot.rs` reads `/Contents`, `/T` and `/M` through it, so every annotation note a conforming producer wrote in PDFDocEncoding came back as MOJIBAKE — on files the operator already has** — ★★★★★ **and the refusal's stated reason had EXPIRED: the comment blamed the spec RAG for not carrying Annex D.3 while `crate::textstring` had carried it in both directions all along** — ★★★★ **mint DECLINED on the strongest grounds this role has filed: the candidate is `R143`'s own written COROLLARY, verbatim in substance, on disk since 2026-08-05; a 2026-08-05 ruling forbids elevating this pattern per occurrence; and the 242nd filing already drafted `R218` for it and caught itself the same way — ★ the candidate's own premise ("no rule covers deferrals") was a stated reason nobody re-checked, making it an instance of the shape it described** — ★★★ **a LIVE stale deferral found by this filing's own sweep, in the same file as its refutation: `format.rs:5003` says "until free-form `Ts` ships (19.2)" while `format.rs:830` IS that function, labelled "(Pass 19.2)" — shipped 2026-08-03, false for 25 days, 4,173 lines apart** — ★★ **the channel check is NOT clean: a new inbound request landed at 03:57, NINETEEN MINUTES BEFORE the 303rd filing's own check, and that filing did not list it because its `ls` was taken at DISPATCH time rather than FILING time** — ★ **and this role's owed-work list decayed in the same commit: it addresses survivors by LINE NUMBER, and `main.rs:3972` is now `:4009`, moved +37 by this Pass's own +76 to that file**

**Shipped:**
- **`Pass 150.0`** (`943d482`) — `MarkupOptions::note: Option<MarkupNote>`,
  writing `/Contents`, `/T` and `/M` (§12.5.2 Table 164; §12.5.6.4 Table 170).
  Lands in `MarkupOptions` so its validation reaches **both** author routes
  through `MarkupOptions::validate` **by construction rather than by whoever
  remembers** — a test asserts the sticky-note route refuses the same malformed
  date the markup route does. An author with no text is allowed; an **empty**
  text is **written rather than omitted**, because a deliberate blank and
  never-having-had-a-note are different document states.
  CLI: `annotate --note TEXT --note-author NAME --note-date D:…`, any one
  sufficing. The long help **states** the no-clock decision and a test asserts
  that by reading `help annotate` — because a caller who does not know pdfce
  refuses to guess will assume it guessed.
- 9 files, **+1,062 / −88** (`git show --numstat`, run here). **486 of 1,062
  changed lines are the three test files — 45.8%**, for a feature whose
  executable half writes three dictionary keys.

**Findings + decisions:**

- **★★★★★ THE READ-SIDE DEFECT, WHICH IS THE HEADLINE.**
  `edit::decode_text_string` did not implement PDFDocEncoding — every non-ASCII
  byte became U+FFFD — and `annot.rs` reads all three note keys through it.
  **PDFDocEncoding is the compact, ordinary choice for Latin text and is what
  Acrobat emits**, so any note carrying an accent, em dash, curly quote, degree
  sign or `Ø` came back corrupt and flagged `exact: false`. **A comment you
  cannot read is a comment you cannot edit.** Fixed by delegating **both**
  `decode_text_string` and `encode_text_string` to `crate::textstring` — one
  implementation of §7.9.2 instead of two that **had already drifted** (one
  answered U+FFFD to bytes the other decoded exactly). `R221`.
- **Why no fixture caught it:** a synthetic fixture carries the bytes its author

## 2026-08-28 (305th filing) — `Pass 151.0` (`c4425f0`) ships `EditSession::resize_annotation` + `pdfce-cli resize-annotation`, the resize half of the transform pair — ★★★★★ **and the Pass exists because THE OPERATOR OVERTURNED AN ANSWER PDFCE HAD ALREADY ACCEPTED FROM ITS OWN CONSUMER**: `pdfceGUI` argued from CAD practice and three reference implementations that stroke width must not scale, pdfce filed that as **settled** in `FEATURES.md`, and Ken ruled it a **default with a toggle** — *"Inkscape has options for this and I want the same"* — ★★★★★ **the generalisable form is a reasoning rule: CONVERGENCE AMONG REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATIONS ARGUES FOR A DEFAULT, NOT AGAINST AN OPTION, and the refutation was inside `pdfceGUI`'s own third argument — Illustrator ships *Scale Strokes & Effects* OFF, which means Illustrator HAS the toggle** — ★★★★ **a bug the engineer wrote and caught in one session, whose first form would have SILENTLY REPLACED ANOTHER PRODUCER'S ARTWORK WITH PDFCE'S RENDERING OF IT and made its own refusal UNREACHABLE** — ★★★ **`ResizeOptions` was UNCONSTRUCTIBLE by any consumer while every in-crate test was green (`#[non_exhaustive]` refuses the struct-expression form outside the defining crate, `..Default::default()` included) — and the RAG file predicting this was written by this role ONE DAY EARLIER, whose prescription is exactly what caught it** — ★★★ **a mirror is an isometry and only the CLI suite found it: `sx = -1` was classified non-uniform, so mirroring a foreign appearance was REFUSED, with all 14 core tests green — per-attribute coverage mistaken for per-combination coverage** — ★★ **hard-rule-11 sweep: `docs/core-api/index.md`'s routing table — the consuming shell's FIRST PAGE — carries FOUR stale figures, and the paragraph directly beneath it is headed *"Every figure above was stale, and the verb count caused an incident"*; the verb count is the only one anybody maintains, because it is the only one with a gate** — ★★ **an `R199` stale blocker found in two places: *"`Pass 46.0`'s own core resize verb (unbuilt)"* has been false since `Pass 134.0`** — ★ **MINT DECLINED, and the dispatch named the SIBLING of the rule that already covers it: `R206`, not `R169`; no decision record either, on decision 094's own stated ground**

**Shipped:**
- **`Pass 151.0`** (`c4425f0`) — `EditSession::resize_annotation(annot_id,
  anchor, sx, sy, &ResizeOptions)` plus the `pdfce-cli resize-annotation`
  subcommand. 10 files, **+2,063 / −6** (`git show --numstat`, run here);
  **944 of 2,063 changed lines are the two new test files — 45.8%**, the same
  ratio `Pass 150.0` filed (486 of 1,062) on a feature a quarter the size.
- New public API in `pdfce-core::edit`: `ResizeOptions` (three flags, `new()`,
  three `with_*` builders), `ResizedAppearance` (4 variants),
  `AnnotationResize` (7 fields), `EditError::ResizeFactorInvalid { axis, value }`,
  `EditError::ResizeAppearanceNotRebuildable { subtype, uniform, why }`,
  `CommandKind::ResizeAnnotation`. `annot_author::read_border_width` widened
  private → `pub(crate)`.
- **Verb count 150 → 151**, verified here by `tools/check-core-api-verbs.py`
  (*"151 public EditSession method(s) in edit.rs … PASS"*). **`EditError`
  variants 88 → 90**, counted here on both sides of the commit.
- New fixture `fixtures/synthetic/annot/rect-differences-square.pdf` (688
  bytes), generated by `tools/gen-annot-fixtures.py` and recorded in that
  directory's `PROVENANCE.md`, both in the same commit.

**Decisions made this session:**
- **Transform side effects are OPTIONS, not answers** (operator ruling,
  2026-08-28). `/RD` scales **by default**; `/BS /W` does **not**; both are
  flags on `ResizeOptions`. **Filed as `R206`'s second instance, NOT as a new
  standing rule and NOT as a decision record** — see the dispositions below.
- **The discriminator behind the two opposite defaults**, stated once so the
  rotate verb inherits it: ***is the property a length in the space being
  transformed?*** An inset is; a line weight is a drafting convention. The same
  test explains why `move_annotation` scales neither — a translation changes no
  length at all.
- **Anchor + factors, never a target `/Rect`** — the shape `transform_objects`
  already takes, so the two transform verbs cannot disagree about what a caller
  supplies. `pdfceGUI` asked for exactly this: *"a verb that took a grip name
  would be encoding our affordance in your crate."*
- **Both refusals reuse `AnnotationMoveWrongVerb`**, deliberately the same
  error type as the move verb, so one `match` arm in a shell covers both
  transform verbs. A parallel `AnnotationResizeWrongVerb` would have been more
  "precise" and would have forced every consumer to write the arm twice.

**Findings + decisions:**
- **★★★★★ The appearance gate, and a bug written and caught in one session.**
  ISO 32000-1 §12.5.5 maps `BBox`×`Matrix` onto `/Rect`. Under a **translation**
  that is a pure translation, so carrying the baked `/AP` is free — which is why
  `Pass 149.0` carries it. Under a **scale** the same mechanism works against
  you: the matrix applies **after** stroking, so the drawn stroke scales
  regardless of `/BS /W`, **anisotropically under a non-uniform scale, which no
  scalar stroke width can express.** The first implementation gated rebuilding
  on `annot_author::spec_from_dict(..).is_ok()` — which asks *"can pdfce PARSE a
  spec out of this dictionary"*, **true of an Acrobat-drawn `/Square` too.** It
  would have silently replaced another producer's artwork with pdfce's rendering
  of it **and** made `ResizeAppearanceNotRebuildable` unreachable. **The
  engineer's own doc comment three lines above forbade exactly that.** The
  shipped gate is `set_markup_style`'s: rebuild from the **unmodified** spec and
  **compare bytes**.
- **★★★ A mirror is an isometry, and only the CLI suite found it.**
  `sx = -1, sy = 1` was classified non-uniform by `(sx - sy).abs()`, so
  mirroring a foreign appearance was **refused**. A reflection preserves every
  length, stroke width included. **All 14 core tests were green while this was
  broken** — no core case had paired a negative factor with a foreign `/AP`.
  Every axis covered, the *combination* not. Uniformity is now tested on `|sx|`
  vs `|sy|`.
- **★★★ `ResizeOptions` was unconstructible by any consumer.**
  `#[non_exhaustive]` refuses the struct-expression form outside the defining
  crate — `..Default::default()` does not exempt you — and is **inert** inside
  it. The three flags would have shipped `pub`, documented, tested and
  **unreachable by the shells they exist for.** Found only because an
  out-of-crate integration test refused to compile. Fixed with `new()` + three
  `with_*` builders, each with a doctest (a doctest being structurally an
  out-of-crate compile). **★ The RAG file predicting this was written by this
  role on 2026-08-27, one day earlier**, and its prescription — *every
  `#[non_exhaustive]` public type gets a test in `tests/`* — is exactly what
  caught it, without anyone consulting the file. **That is the best outcome a
  RAG entry can have** and is recorded as such rather than as a near-miss.
- **★★ The second-order hole, where the next silence would come from.**
  `#[non_exhaustive]` on the **outcome** enum forces a `_` arm on the CLI's
  match, and its compulsory empty form `_ => {}` is precisely how a future
  variant ships as silence. **Both `_` arms in the CLI are written to SPEAK.**
  The attribute that protects the library's evolution manufactures, at every
  consumer, a hole shaped exactly like a rule-4 disclosure gap.
- **★★ A raw Python string ships `\u2014` into Rust, and Rust catches it in one
  place and not the other.** `r'''…'''` passes the escape through verbatim; in a
  **string literal** that is a hard compile error, in a **`///` doc comment** it
  compiles silently and ships as wrong `--help` text. **17 instances, all in doc
  comments — because the ones in literals stopped the build and were fixed
  individually, turning the build green, which is the signal that means "class
  cleared". A partly-loud defect class is more dangerous than a wholly-silent
  one.** Verified here in a throwaway crate, both halves. Repair script
  `D:/Dev/temp/pdfce/fixesc.py`; detection regex
  `re.compile(r"\\u([0-9a-fA-F]{4})(?!\})")`, the `}` lookahead sparing genuine
  `\u{FFFD}`. **Residual tree-wide scan run here: 2 hits, both correct** — a doc
  comment describing **JavaScript's** `\uD800` and a raw byte-string test of a
  JS escape, in `crates/pdfce-core/src/form_script/shape.rs`. The regex cannot
  tell a `\uXXXX` being *used* from one being *quoted*.
- **★ The flag-wiring check, and why it is its own verification row.** Unit
  tests build their own `ResizeOptions` and call core directly, so **a flag
  parsed by `clap` and then dropped before the call passes every one of them.**
  Each CLI flag is therefore proved by running the **same resize twice**, with
  and without, requiring the **saved bytes** to differ in the key that flag
  owns. **This and the `ResizeOptions` finding are the same defect at two
  scales** — an option no consumer can set, and an option a consumer sets that
  nothing reads. Both invisible to a green suite; both caught by **leaving the
  crate**.
- **The fixture is the gate's only falsifier.**
  `rect-differences-square.pdf` is the **only** fixture carrying `/RD`, and its
  `/AP` is foreign to pdfce **by construction** — which is what makes *"pdfce
  will not redraw somebody else's artwork"* measurable rather than asserted. Its
  four `/RD` values are deliberately **unequal**, because Table 175 orders them
  **[left, top, right, bottom]** and an implementation reading `[x, y, x, y]`
  looks correct on any fixture whose values match.

**Dispositions — nothing minted, and both declines are argued:**

  the dispatch supposed. `R169` is deliberately scoped to *"bucket-1 SETTING

  the occurrence count:** a second rule saying *"and remember convergence only

  general over **all** evidence for a default. `R169`/`R206` are already a

## 2026-08-28 (306th filing) — `Pass 143.0` ships in `4094e49` and the `check-core-api-verbs` gate extension in `3dc9eb0`: ★★★★★ **the Backlog entry's own *Cause* was WRONG, and only an A/B of the rendered pixels could say so — the filed cause was implemented exactly as written, compiled, was instrumented and demonstrably REACHED, and moved ZERO PIXELS**; ★★★★★ **the print-conformance corpus is a POOR ORACLE for this defect — and this entry's first version said BLIND, on a scan taken between the two halves of the fix; corrected the same day to 3 of 51 patches changing pixels and 0 of 3 changing verdict, so the entry's "back to 5 FAIL or better" was still UNREACHABLE and the failing patch's remaining traps still have a different, unknown cause**; ★★★★ **and the FILED SYMPTOM was stale too — the surround it named reads 81,119,40 under both settings and it is the TRAP X that is wrong**; ★★★ **two agreeing copies of one predicate CANCELLED EACH OTHER UNDER SABOTAGE** (`R221`'s fourth instance); ★★★★★ **and this filing's own sweep found that the 2026-08-25 operator ruling keeping the licensed suite's name out of this public repository is VIOLATED IN 83 COMMIT MESSAGES, 82 ALREADY PUSHED — a surface the gate cannot see and never could**

**Shipped:**
- **`Pass 143.0` (`4094e49`)** — `pdfce_core::settings::OverprintZeroTintScope`,
  three values (`device_cmyk_only` / **`grey_as_k_only`, default** /
  `all_process_spaces`), threaded through `Settings` (parse **and**
  `write_to_string`), `RenderOptions::with_overprint_zero_tint_scope`,
  `RenderPolicy`, `pdfce-cli render-page --overprint-zero-tint-scope`, and a
  control in `crates/pdfce-gui`'s settings panel. **A `DeviceGray` fill
  overprinting a spot backdrop now PRESERVES it by default** instead of
  knocking it out. **16 files, +1,153 / −18**; **538 of 1,153 changed lines are
  the test file and the fixture generator — 46.7 %**, the third consecutive
  Pass within one point of that ratio.
- **`3dc9eb0`** — `tools/check-core-api-verbs.py` extended to gate the four
  figures in `docs/core-api/index.md` that had none, discharging the 305th
  filing's *"the fix is to extend the gate, not to ask for more care."*
  **2 files, +82 / −3.**

**Findings + decisions:**

- **★★★★★ THE FILED DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, AND THE WAY IT WAS WRONG IS THE
  LESSON.** The Backlog entry named `overprint::classify` mapping `DeviceGray`
  to `SourceKind::OtherProcess`. The engineer implemented exactly that: it
  compiled, it was **instrumented and demonstrably reached** (`converts=true`
  on 10 paints), the classification demonstrably changed — **and it moved zero
  pixels**, on the fixtures and on all 51 conformance patches. The real gate
  was `Interpreter::overprint_would_change`, whose `_ => false` arm carried a
  comment calling it *"a known under-count rather than a claim of zero"* —
  **true of the DISCLOSURE, and the sentence did not say the same arm also
  gated the BEHAVIOUR.** ⇒ **Reaching the code is not the same as changing the
  result.** A correct-looking, compiling, demonstrably-reached change that
  moves no pixels is **indistinguishable from a right fix waiting on something
  else**; nothing separates the two but rendering both binaries and diffing.
  Filed as a dated clause **(f)** on `R219`, whose 295th-filing amendment
  already carried the route-level form of the same fact.
- **★★★★★ THE CONFORMANCE CORPUS IS A POOR ORACLE FOR THIS DEFECT —
  AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS BULLET SAID *BLIND*, ON A NUMBER MEASURED
  BEFORE THE FIX EXISTED.** ~~Instrumenting `cmyk_group_rules` across all 51
  patches: **zero** paint a `DeviceGray` source through Table 149. The patch
  whose *name* promises exactly that case authors its greys as `DeviceCMYK
  [0 0 0 k]`, which always took the direct-CMYK row.~~ **That scan ran after
  the `classify` change and BEFORE the `overprint_would_change` fix — and
  `overprint_would_change` is the predicate whose fix makes greys reach
  Table 149 — so it measured the DEFECT, not the FIX**, and was carried across
  the very commit that invalidated it. Corrected by the engineer on `4094e49`,
  by rendering every patch **twice with the shipped binary**
  (`--overprint-zero-tint-scope device_cmyk_only`, which reproduces the
  pre-Pass behaviour exactly, vs. the default) and counting differing pixels:
  **3 of 51 change — 8,491 (a font-support patch, passes under both), 1,827
  (the grey/K-black overprint patch, FAILs under both), 804 (the
  white-overprint patch, FAILs under both) — and 0 of 3 change verdict.**
  ⇒ The three consequences **survive with a weaker reason**: the entry's
  *"back to 5 FAIL or better"* was **unreachable by this fix and not because
  the fix is wrong**; the suite is unchanged at **6 FAIL / 29 pass / 16
  unresolved of 51** (no regression, **no improvement the corpus could
  score**); and the failing patch's remaining **3 traps have a different,
  still-unknown cause** — an open item, previously misattributed.
  **★ A claim the corrected figure CONTRADICTS**, flagged not dropped: that
  patch is the 1,827-pixel row, and pixels move only if a **non-`DeviceCMYK`**
  source reached the zero-tint rule, so *"authors its greys as `DeviceCMYK
  [0 0 0 k]`"* cannot be a complete account of it. **Unestablished pending the
  engineer's re-read of the content stream** — not asserted either way here.
- **★★★★ AND THE FILED *SYMPTOM* HAD ALREADY BEEN FIXED — a second,
  separate correction, and an `R199` instance about the DEFECT REPORT rather
  than about a blocker.** The retired Backlog entry said the patch's surround
  read **127,127,127** against Acrobat's **84,120,34**. That was measured at
  **`70c5919`**, several Passes ago. Re-probed on `4094e49` with
  `tools/suite-cell-probe.py`: the **surround reads 81,119,40 under BOTH
  settings** — already within a few levels of Acrobat *before* this Pass,
  under the literal reading — and what is still wrong is the **trap X**, at
  **127,127,127** against a green surround. ⇒ **The entry carried a stale
  SYMPTOM as well as a wrong CAUSE**, and the two have different remedies: a
  wrong cause is corrected by measuring the **fix's effect**, a stale symptom
  by **re-measuring the defect**. Nothing in this project re-measures a filed
  symptom before the Pass that closes it.
- **★★★★ THE ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE IS ORACLE-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION.**
  `tools/gen-grey-overprint-fixtures.py` builds five fixtures.
  `grey_op_over_spot.pdf` and `cmyk_k_op_over_spot.pdf` differ in **exactly one
  way** — `0.5 g` versus `0 0 0 0.5 k`, the same ink stated twice — so *"treat
  grey as the K-only CMYK it converts to"* **means** they must land on
  identical pixels. Measured: grey **(127,127,127) → (13,90,47)**, exactly
  equal to the CMYK reference. No remembered colour, no reference engine, no
  threshold (`R215`).
- **★★★ TWO COPIES OF ONE PREDICATE CANCELLED EACH OTHER OUT** — `R221`'s
  fourth instance, and the first where the copies **agreed**. The first cut
  gave `overprint_would_change` its own `overprint_scope_covers` helper; a
  deliberate sabotage (widening `grey_as_k_only` to every space) **survived
  because `classify`'s copy still refused.** ⇒ *A redundant predicate does not
  merely risk drift; it **suppresses the sabotage** that would have found it* —
  breaking either copy alone produces no observable change, so neither is
  covered by any test. Removed; the predicate now asks `classify`.
- **★★ A TEST'S DOC COMMENT CLAIMED COVERAGE IT DID NOT HAVE, AND THE TEST IS
  FINE.** Three sabotages proved false a comment claiming the test pinned the
  `!in_image_sample` guard — a grey source inside a sampled image never enters
  the overprint machinery at all, protected redundantly three ways. **Comment
  corrected, test kept.** ⇒ *A surviving sabotage sometimes means the COMMENT's
  coverage claim is wrong, not that the TEST is weak*, and **the two have
  opposite remedies** (rewrite the sentence vs. write another test). Mint
  declined at n = 1; adjacency note and revisit trigger recorded at `R223`.
- **★★ FOUR GATES CAUGHT REAL OMISSIONS ON THE FIRST SWEEP**, which is an
  argument for running the whole set rather than the expected ones:
  `check-settings-consumed.py` (**`write_to_string` was missing — saving
  settings would have silently dropped the new one**; the engineer did not know
  this gate existed), `check-string-gaps.sh` (two eaten Rust line-continuations
  in the new test file), the GUI settings-panel reachability test (a setting
  with no control), and the `RenderPolicy` projection test — **whose builder
  call was also missing, so it would have passed while the builder did
  nothing.** That last is `Pass 151.0`'s flag-wiring finding one layer down.
- **★★ `3dc9eb0`: NORMALISING THE FORMAT WAS A PREREQUISITE FOR GATING THE
  CONTENT.** The routing table's three rows carried three different shapes
  (*"N lines · N verified citations"*, *"N lines · N citations"*, bare *"N
  lines"*), and **a gate can only be written against a shape present in every
  row** — the heterogeneity was the thing blocking enforcement, not
  untidiness. Corrected figures: `EditError` **88 → 90**; part 1 **2,223 →
  2,649**; part 2 **1,550 → 2,999** (the stale figure was **51.7 %** of the
  truth); part 3 **2,079 → 2,533**. **★ The *"128 citations"* claim could not
  be verified even in principle** — clause refs **73**, distinct **47**,
  `file.rs:line` citations **186** — so *a number nobody can re-derive is a
  number nobody can check*, which **is the mechanism of the drift**. Replaced
  with a gate-derived *"N clauses cited"*. Verified by three sabotage runs, all
  caught; **★ the first cut of the check went GREEN while matching no rows at
  all** — *a gate that checks nothing also prints PASS* (`R224`'s vacuous-scan
  clause, recurring in `tools/` the day it was minted).

**★★★★★ WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND THAT NEITHER COMMIT TOUCHED — read this first:**

The 2026-08-25 operator ruling (open question `(bt)`,
`tools/check-suite-name-absent.py`) keeps the licensed print-conformance
suite's name **out of this public repository entirely — file contents AND file
names.** It is satisfied in both. **It is violated in COMMIT MESSAGES.**
Measured by this role by decoding the gate's own base64 needles and scanning
`git log --format=%B --all`, **without ever printing or writing the term**:

| measurement | result |
|---|---|
| commits whose **message** contains a forbidden needle | **83** |
| of those, already **pushed** | **82** (`origin/main` = `25004cd`) |
| **unpushed** | **1** — `4094e49`, this Pass, one occurrence |
| work-tree contents and file names | **clean**, `python tools/check-suite-name-absent.py` → exit 0 |

**The gate cannot see commit messages and never could** — its own docstring
scopes it to *"file CONTENTS … and file NAMES"*. **This is not a gate that
failed; it is a rule enforced over half its own surface**, and the unenforced
half was already breached at scale before the gate was written. **Filed, not
fixed:** removing 82 published messages is a rewrite of published history,
which rule 8 gates behind an explicit operator go-ahead and which this project
has costed evidence against (`tools/check-cited-commits-exist.py`, `0d9f4df`,
fourteen casualties). **The operator's call.** ★ Note the shape: every
refinement the gate received — base64 needles, masked output, untracked files
included — is about the two surfaces it already covered, and *"the gate is
green"* has been read as *"the ruling is satisfied"* for three days. **A gate's
silence is only as wide as its input set, and its input set is the one thing
its output never states.**

### ★★★★★ THE FINDING — EVERYTHING ASKED FOR ALREADY WORKED, AND THE ENUMERATION IS THE FINDING

Four independent facts, each verified before the constructor was written:

1. **Behaviour** — an empty `find` with a pin has meant *"the whole pinned show
   operator"* on `edit_text` since `Pass 145.0`; `edit.rs:1643` calls
   `effective_find`, the same resolver three sibling entry points call.
2. **Test** — `whole_operator_pin.rs::edit_text_gets_the_same_affordance`
   already existed and was already green.
3. **Disclosure** — it already emitted the rule-4 off-canvas disclosure naming
   the extent taken **and** the multi-operator caveat; the engineer verified it
   on the CLI (**11 characters, three disclosures printed**).
4. **Shell** — `pdfce-cli edit-text --pin-span` with no `--find` already worked,
   and that subcommand's `--find` help documents the empty case at three sites
   (`main.rs:1956`, `:4365`, `:4511`), all correct.

⇒ **Nothing in this project could have detected the failure.** There is no gate
for *"a true sentence nobody can act on"*. `tools/run-gates.sh` was **PASS over
26 commands** while the defect was live. **The only symptom this failure has is
a consuming project filing a request for a capability it already possesses** —
a signal that arrives through the request channel, late, and only if the
consumer asks instead of building a workaround.

### ★★★★★ WHAT THE DOCUMENT SAID, AND WHY READING IT DID NOT HELP

The edit half was there, in full:

> *"`EditRequest` gets the same affordance by setting `pinned_span` with an
> empty `find`."*

**True. Accurate. Right file. Right section — the block their report cites by
name.** Three properties it lacked, each separately fatal: **no symbol** (grep
`whole_operator` returns `FormatRequest`'s only); **no example** (the reader
must compose `find_replace(page, "", replace)` with `.pinned(span)` from prose
that never says `find_replace`); **position under a heading naming the other
type**.

Having read it, they filed a defect saying a pinned `edit_text` **can only** be
addressed by `find`, and listed **three attempts to reconstruct a `find`** for
an operator they had already located — on the operator's own CAD drawing, where
`text_extract`'s synthesised inter-glyph spacing (**twenty-one spaces**, not in
the content stream) means a rebuilt `find` can **never** match. They were doing
the hardest available version of a thing that was already unnecessary.

The 306th filing opened a box whose heading read *"`format_text` was made
addressable by PIN ALONE and its sibling `edit_text` was not"*, called it
`R219`'s shape, and framed the open question as *"whether `edit_text` **gains**

**The mechanism of the error is `R220`(e), minted one filing earlier.** The
requester supplied a **symptom** they had reproduced (`pdfce-diag
edit-text-refused`, twenty-one synthesised spaces, a pin set the whole time) —
good evidence, every particular of which held. In the same paragraph they

cheapest claim in this codebase to check, and `R220`(c) already says to check
it. **`grep -n "effective_find" crates/pdfce-core/src/text_edit/edit.rs` would
have answered in under a minute.** Nobody ran it, because the requester had
said so and nobody doubted them. **Caught by the engineer running the CLI**,
not by any gate, not by any re-reading, and not by this role's own
hard-rule-11 sweep in the filing that created it.

### THE DECLINE — HONOURING THE PIN OVER A NON-EMPTY `find`

`pdfceGUI`'s option 2, which **they flagged themselves** as a silent contract
change. Declined on a capability rather than on caution: with a non-empty
`find` the pin narrows **which operator** and the find narrows **which
characters within it**. *"Replace `Rev A` with `Rev B`, but only in this one
show operator"* is coherent, useful, and has no other spelling. Making the pin
outrank the find would delete that combination silently, from every existing
caller, with no error.

### ★ MINTING — `R220` AMENDED IN PLACE (CLAUSE (f)), NOTHING MINTED, `R197` DECLINED AS CARRIER

**Clause (f):** *a capability's documentation carries a **SYMBOL** a reader can
grep and a **SNIPPET** a reader can paste — never only a true sentence
describing how to spell it out of other parts.* Where two verbs answer the same
question, **both are named**; *"X gets the same affordance by …"* is the defect
the clause catches, and its remedy is a **name**, not more prose.

**Why `R220` and not a mint.** `R220` **is** the findability rule, minted
2026-08-27 from an incident of this exact shape. This is its **fifth instance
and its sharpest**: in instances 1 and 2 the entry was in the wrong document or
indexed by the wrong mechanism, and a reader could fairly be said not to have
found it. **Here the reader found it, read it, cited it, and still could not
act on it** — a claim about the **FORM** an entry takes, which (a) and (b) do
not reach. By (d)'s own stated test, *"a rule whose remedy duplicates an
existing rule's is a clause"*. `R220` has precedent: (d) and (e) were both
added in place in one filing without moving the ceiling.

**Why `R197` was declined as the carrier** (the dispatch's suggestion, offered
without proposing a mint). `R197`'s subject is a **figure's shelf life**.
**Nothing here is a figure, nothing was stale, and the sentence was true at
`HEAD` on the day it was read** — an anchor would have changed nothing. The
dispatch's analogy points at `R197`'s **minting incident**, not its **rule**;
**a rule is its text, not its founding story**, and widening `R197` toward
findability would destroy the exhaustive scope enumeration that makes it
checkable.

**Why (f) is not "write better docs".** The failing sentence was **maximally
good prose** — shorter, more accurate and more precise than what replaced it.
**Prose quality was not the variable.** The variable was whether the text
carried a **token that survives `grep`** and a **fragment that survives paste**
— properties a reviewer checks **mechanically at write time, without
judgement**.

**No gate**, on `R220`'s own founding reasoning: *"findability is not a
property any script can evaluate."*

**Ceiling unmoved: rules stay at `R224`, next free `R225`** — confirmed by
`python tools/check-ledger-numbers.py`, run after these edits. **Revisit
trigger, adopted from the dispatch as written: a third occurrence where the
remedy is a SYMBOL rather than more prose.**

**No decision record.** Nothing architectural was decided. Decision **094**
remains newest; next free **095**.

### ★★ `NeutralBlack`'s reasoning did not stop being true

Pure `0 0 0 1 k` still renders `#231F20` under the new default and that is
still not what a CAD operator expects. **`NeutralBlack` remains available and
remains the right answer for drawings.** What changed is which of two
defensible `R169`/`R206` answers ships first, not the evidence. **A future
session finding a drawing's blacks "wrong" should reach for the setting, not
file a defect** — the type docs now say that in those words.

### ★★★ A note that died with its divergence

`pdfce-gui` carried *"pdfce's default deliberately differs from Acrobat here"*
at that setting, placed so a render-parity difference would not be investigated
as a defect. **With the default matching, that sentence is not redundant — it
is backwards**, and would send the next reader hunting a difference that is not
there. **Deleted, not reworded**, along with the long "knowingly diverges"
argument in `CmykIntent`'s type docs and two passages of `settings_panel`'s
module docs. `pdfceGUI` reached the same conclusion independently and deleted
theirs.

The generalisable half survives because it outlived its example, and is kept:
**a doc comment that describes a default as a DIVERGENCE invites being read as
a divergence in VALUE** — state the shipped default and the best-evidenced
answer as two lines of data, and **when they agree, say so**, because an absent
statement reads as an unexamined one. That is `a3185ba`'s finding (265th
filing), restated by the event that removed its example — **and its second
clause is exactly what the Pass then failed to do**, see the sweep.

### `Naive` — a control whose justification expired in silence

It existed so an operator could reproduce a pre-calibration pdfce export. True
when written, and it stopped being true as those files aged out — **with no
test failing, no gate firing, and the copy still reading sensibly.** A control
whose only purpose is bug-compatibility with your own past **has no failure
mode**, so it is removable only by somebody deciding to. `pdfceGUI` filed the
shape as *"an option justified by a transitional need needs a review date."*

It survives in `color/mod.rs`'s *"what was rejected, and why it is recorded
here"* list. A stored `cmyk_intent = naive` now hits the bad-value path and is
**reported** — verified by running it. Deleting the parse arm rather than
silently accepting the dead token is the rule-4 choice.

### ★★★★★ `--fix`, and the cut that read the wrong file

`index.md`'s routing table carries three *"N lines · N clauses cited"*
figures. They are **derived, not decided** — nothing chooses them, they are a
function of the file — so the gate that already derives them to *check* them
can also **write** them. The prompt was mechanical: those figures were
hand-re-derived **three times in one session**.

**The finding is the first cut, not the feature.** It anchored on `VERB_INDEX`
(`02-editing-and-saving.md`) — the document the table **points at** — while
the table lives in `index.md`, the document that **contains** it. One
hyperlink apart, interchangeable at a glance.

- **Zero rows matched, zero rewritten, clean exit.** *"Nothing needed fixing"*
  and *"I was looking at the wrong file"* are byte-identical output.
- **Every surrounding filter passed and the regex was correct**, so the
  symptom pointed at the one component that was not at fault — three
  debugging rounds on the regex.
- **★ The near-miss: had it matched, it would have written `index.md`'s size
  figures into `02-editing-and-saving.md`.** A vacuous reader prints a false
  PASS; a vacuous **writer** is one successful match from corrupting the file
  it was mistakenly pointed at.

**Verified by sabotage** — the positive control the first cut lacked: a figure
corrupted to `9,999` is repaired to the derived value, the file returns
**byte-identical** to its pre-sabotage state, and a second run rewrites **0**.
That test cannot pass on an empty subject set, which is precisely the property
that was missing.

**★ A flag, not automatic.** *A gate that repairs the tree it audits cannot be
trusted to report on it* — CI must still see red.

### Minting — a second dated note on `R224`, no mint

Recorded under `R224` in `ROADMAP.md`'s *Standing rules*. This is the ★★
vacuous-scan clause at its **second `tools/` instance in three days, on the
same script and the same document** (the first, `3dc9eb0`, is already noted
there by the 306th filing). Two things are new and are why it earned a second
note rather than nothing:

- **The anchor was not renamed — it was wrong from birth.** The clause is
  phrased around decay (*"its anchor is renamed"*). This one never worked and
  looked identical to working on every run. *Vacuous is not only what a scan
  decays into; it is also what a scan can be born in.*
- **A vacuous WRITER is a near-miss, not an uninformative report** ⇒ *every
  `--fix` owes a positive control that its subject set is non-empty, and owes
  it more than a read-only gate does.*

**Mint declined; ceiling stays `R224`, next free `R225`.** The subject is the
existing clause's own — *any assertion whose subject set can be empty* — and
n = 2 in one tree does not buy a number when the rule already covers it. This
follows the 306th filing's disposition unchanged.

**No decision-log entry.** `180f19f` changes no architecture, defines no
invariant and moves no crate boundary. It corrects claims *about* a decision
(**095**) that already stands, and adds a maintenance flag to an existing
gate.
